meta.subject: Enlisted men of Capt. Nathan Heald's company, 1st US Infantry, Fort Dearborn, 1812
meta.caution: Facts are only those quoted. Enlistment dates come from the Dec 1810 roll (Wentworth via Kirkland); name-matching to the May 1812 roll is noted where spellings differ. Heritage hints from forenames are interpretation, not evidence.

height.population: Native-born white US Army recruits enlisting 1815-1820, aged 24-35 (regional means by Quantile Bend, weighted by census population shares). Regional: Middle Atlantic 67.9 (n=1,018), New England 68.0 (668), South 68.3 (477). Revolutionary-era recruits: also 68.1 (n=968).
height.source_title: The Heights of Americans in Three Centuries: Some Economic and Demographic Implications (NBER Working Paper 1384), Table 1, drawing on Sokoloff & Villaflor, "The Early Achievement of Modern Stature in America", Social Science History 6 (Fall 1982)
height.author: Kenneth L. Sokoloff
height.quote: U.S. Army, 1815—1820 67.9 68.0 68.3 68.1 / Aged 24—35 (1,018) (668) (477) (2,163)  …  "a figure of 68.3 inches, which slightly exceeds the 68.1 inch estimates calculated for both the Revolutionary War period and the years 1815—1820."
height.sd_note: Neither Sokoloff 1984 nor the abstract of Sokoloff & Villaflor 1982 reachable online states a standard deviation (the 1982 article itself is paywalled; I could not verify its text). SD computed by me from two transcribed War of 1812 register samples (raw, not truncation-corrected): (a) Maine 1812 database, army only, ages 24-35: mean 68.74 in, SD 2.54, n=354, range 61.5-75.5; ages 21-45: mean 68.62, SD 2.47, n=811. (b) 22nd US Infantry dead/missing transcribed from M233 (mostly Pennsylvania-born): mean 68.71 in, SD 2.44, n=171, range 61-75. Raw sample means exceed Sokoloff's 68.1 partly because recruiting minimum-height rules and rounding are not corrected for. A working value of SD ≈ 2.5 in is supported by both samples.

base_rates.notes: Fort Dearborn's company was 1st US Infantry, enlisted mostly 1805-1810 (Kirkland/Wentworth roll), i.e. pre-war recruits, likely from the Ohio valley/mid-Atlantic/south rather than New England; the 22nd Infantry (PA) sample is probably the closer analogue, the Maine sample the larger one. Both are register samples of the War of 1812 era, not of Heald's men. not_found: Register of Enlistments (NARA M233) entries for any of the 51 men: no transcription found online. The registers are on Ancestry/Fold3/FamilySearch (FamilySearch collection 1880762) behind logins; could not consult. Searched genealogy pages, WikiTree, Find a Grave, Fold3 memorial snippets.

Quaife 1913 Appendix VIII (full text checked): names, ranks and fates only — no age, birthplace or description. Quaife: "With the exception of Grummo, no record has been found of the further career of these men" (of the nine returned via Quebec, p.239).
Kirkland 1893 (full text checked): reprints the Dec 1810 muster roll (names, rank, enlistment dates, remarks) — no descriptions.
Helm 1814 / Gordon 1912 (full text checked): lists survivors and fates; no descriptions apart from Griffith "Supposed to be a Frenchman".

James Van Horne, "A narrative of the captivity & sufferings of James Van Horne…" (Middlebury, Vt., 1817; HathiTrust mdp.39015071158490, full view): could not read — HathiTrust page blocked automated access (Cloudflare). May contain his birthplace/origin; worth checking by hand.
Currey, "The Story of Old Fort Dearborn" (1912) text download failed (proxy 502); not checked. Andreas 1884 and Musham 1943 not checked for individual descriptions in this pass.
David Kennison: the Maine-archives 1813 record for "David Kennison" (b. New Durham NH, age 26, 6 ft, light, blue, dark) is a different man — excluded.
Paul Grummo/De Garmo: no genealogy found for a Paul DeGarmo of Maumee; the Valley of the Upper Maumee (1905) full text has no mention.

Otho Hays, Isaac Holt, Fielding/James Corbin, Nathan Edson, Dyson Dyer, Micajah Denison, Prestly Andrews, Rhodias Jones, Joseph Bowen, John Crozier: targeted searches found no birthplace or description.

Standard deviation of height: not found stated in Sokoloff 1984; Sokoloff & Villaflor 1982 full text paywalled (could not verify any SD in it). SD given above is my computation from transcribed samples.

Published distribution of complexion/eye/hair colour among 1812-era enlistees: no study found. Brenckle 2025 (USS Constitution Marines) gives only a composite "blue eyes, brown hair, and a fair complexion".

Surname references: Ancestry (Hanks DAFN 2003) pages and some forebears.io pages were blocked (Cloudflare/403); used forebears.io quotations of older dictionaries (Bardsley 1896, Harrison 1912, Black 1946, E. C. Smith DAFN 1956, MacLysaght 1964) and the Internet Surname Database instead. No reference reached for Kennison, Suttenfield or Sherror.

Portraits: several Met candidates (Ammi Phillips "Philip Slade" 1818, Jarvis "Portrait of a Gentleman" 1809, Jennys "Gentleman of the Hale Family" c.1807, Waldo "Old Pat, the Independent Beggar" c.1819 and "Portrait of a Man" c.1820) are served only as black-and-white photographs, so excluded. No painted portrait of a US enlisted soldier of 1812 found. Wikimedia Commons API was rate-limited, so Commons items (e.g. Neagle, "Pat Lyon at the Forge") were not checked. NGA Eichholtz "Henry Eichholtz Leman" (c.1835) is not downloadable.
